name: Leg Weave
description: Leg Weave is a passing control in which the top player threads an arm between the guard player's legs and controls the lower thigh or knee, bringing the knees together to clear the guard.
variant_uniqueness: Arm weave joins the knees for a guard pass
summary: Leg Weave is a passing control in which the top player threads an arm between the guard player's legs and controls the lower thigh or knee, bringing the knees together to clear the guard.
overview:
The bottom player has a knee shield or comparable leg frame between the bodies. The top player's arm travels between the legs and controls the lower thigh or knee. Shoulder pressure and the arm connection bring the knees closer together. The passer retains a base while working to clear the remaining foot or half-guard hook.

The weaving limb is the passer's arm. The passer still moves the feet and hips to clear the guard, but threading a shin through the legs is not the defining weave in this instruction. Terminology: Arm-weave passing control, Leg-weave control.

Thread the arm through the available leg gap and connect to the lower thigh or knee. Use aligned shoulder and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint. Avoid leaving the weaving arm extended where the bottom player can sit up into a kimura.

Apply gradual body pressure and move the hip with the leg. Avoid forcing a planted knee sideways or leaving the weaving arm extended under a sudden kimura counter.

Instructional sources: [Lachlan Giles — leg weave pass, no gi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9rDzchSk4fw); [Lachlan Giles — leg-weave counter demonstration](https://bjjfanatics.com/blogs/news/interesting-leg-weave-counter-with-lachlan-giles).
key_principles: Weave the arm: Thread the arm through the available leg gap and connect to the lower thigh or knee.
Manage the knee shield: Use aligned shoulder and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint.
Keep the elbow protected: Avoid leaving the weaving arm extended where the bottom player can sit up into a kimura.
Maintain an outside base: Move the hips and feet without collapsing all weight over the woven arm.
Clear the legs before settling: Remove the remaining foot or half-guard hook before establishing side control.
Follow the hips: If the bottom player turns or inserts a frame, keep control of distance and reset the pass rather than forcing a fixed angle.

flashcards.question: Leg Weave passing: what contact completes the arm route through the leg gap?
flashcards.answer: Thread the arm through the available leg gap and connect to the lower thigh or knee.

plausible: The upper ankle while leaving the two knees separated
The far hip with neither thigh contained by the forearm
trap: The top of the shield with no arm through the leg gap

flashcards.question: Leg Weave passing: how should you compress a knee shield?
flashcards.answer: Use aligned shoulder and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint.
flashcards.answer_line: Fold the knees with connected chest/shoulder pressure

plausible: Twist the upper foot while the knee stays fixed
Push the upper knee away from the lower thigh
trap: Drop the shoulder behind the shield without connecting the legs

flashcards.question: Leg Weave passing: which two arm contacts become available for a kimura if your elbow drifts out?
flashcards.answer: An exposed weaving arm lets the guard player control the wrist and encircle the elbow for a kimura grip. Keep the elbow connected instead of leaving a long isolated lever.
flashcards.answer_line: The wrist and the space around the elbow

plausible: The biceps and shoulder without access to the wrist
The forearm shaft with no route around the elbow
trap: The back of the hand while the elbow remains sealed to the ribs

flashcards.question: Leg Weave passing: how do you stay balanced while moving past the legs?
flashcards.answer: Move the hips and feet without collapsing all weight over the woven arm.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep an outside base as your hips and feet move

plausible: Stack all your weight directly over the weaving wrist
Bring both feet together beneath the opponent's knees
trap: Stop moving the hips and pull only with the arm

flashcards.question: Leg Weave passing: what must happen before you settle into side control?
flashcards.answer: Remove the remaining foot or half-guard hook before establishing side control.
flashcards.answer_line: Clear the remaining foot or half-guard hook

plausible: Touch your chest to the opponent's shoulder
Place your forehead beside their ear
trap: Join your knees while their foot still catches your leg

flashcards.question: Leg Weave passing: the opponent turns and reintroduces a frame; what is the useful adjustment?
flashcards.answer: If the bottom player turns or inserts a frame, keep control of distance and reset the pass rather than forcing a fixed angle.
flashcards.answer_line: Follow the hips, manage distance and reset the angle

plausible: Keep the same angle and twist their knee harder
Abandon your base to yank the woven leg inward
trap: Drive straight ahead while your arm stays stretched

flashcards.question: Leg Weave passing: what obstacle is usually between the two bodies at the start?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player has a knee shield or comparable leg frame between the bodies.
flashcards.answer_line: A knee shield or similar leg frame

plausible: Knees collapsed outside the passer with no shin between the torsos
Both feet withdrawn while the passer has already cleared the leg line
trap: A settled chest-to-chest pin with neither knee still between the bodies

flashcards.question: Leg Weave passing: which limb makes the defining weave?
flashcards.answer: The weaving limb is the passer's arm. The passer still moves the feet and hips to clear the guard, but threading a shin through the legs is not the defining weave in this instruction.
flashcards.answer_line: Your arm threaded between their legs

plausible: Your shin cutting across the opponent's shield knee
Your feet stepping around the knees while the arms stay outside
trap: Your foot pummeling under the upper shin

bottom.name: Leg Weave Bottom
bottom.description: Leg Weave bottom perspective: The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip. Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together.
bottom.overview:
The bottom player is responsible for recognizing and defending the control. The bottom player has a knee shield or comparable leg frame between the bodies. The top player's arm travels between the legs and controls the lower thigh or knee. Shoulder pressure and the arm connection bring the knees closer together. The passer retains a base while working to clear the remaining foot or half-guard hook.

The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip. Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together. Move the hips and pummel the knee back between the bodies while the weave is still loose.

Prevent the passer from flattening your shoulders while controlling the legs. An underhook can help you face the passer and rebuild half guard when the shoulder line is not already pinned. Do not wrench a knee out of a fixed weave; create room with the hips and frames first.

The weaving limb is the passer's arm. The passer still moves the feet and hips to clear the guard, but threading a shin through the legs is not the defining weave in this instruction. Apply gradual body pressure and move the hip with the leg. Avoid forcing a planted knee sideways or leaving the weaving arm extended under a sudden kimura counter.
state_invariants: The bottom player has a knee shield or comparable leg frame between the bodies.
The top player's arm travels between the legs and controls the lower thigh or knee.
Shoulder pressure and the arm connection bring the knees closer together.
The passer retains a base while working to clear the remaining foot or half-guard hook.
prerequisites: The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip.
Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together.
Move the hips and pummel the knee back between the bodies while the weave is still loose.
key_principles: Recognize the arm weave: The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip.
Keep the shield supported: Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together.
Recover inside space: Move the hips and pummel the knee back between the bodies while the weave is still loose.
Deny upper-body collapse: Prevent the passer from flattening your shoulders while controlling the legs.
Use an available underhook: An underhook can help you face the passer and rebuild half guard when the shoulder line is not already pinned.
Move the whole leg: Do not wrench a knee out of a fixed weave; create room with the hips and frames first.

flashcards.question: Leg Weave defense: what directly connects your two knees during the pass?
flashcards.answer: The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip.
flashcards.answer_line: The passer's arm through your leg gap

plausible: The passer's chest pin with no arm through the leg gap
An outside hip block that leaves the knees separated
trap: A crossface without the lower-body threading connection

flashcards.question: Leg Weave defense: what helps keep the shield useful before the passer folds your legs?
flashcards.answer: Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together.
flashcards.answer_line: Support the knee angle with an upper-body frame

plausible: Let both knees collapse toward the mat
Push only with the shield foot and turn the knee inward
trap: Reach both arms behind the passer's back

flashcards.question: Leg Weave defense: while the weave is loose, how can you regain inside space?
flashcards.answer: Move the hips and pummel the knee back between the bodies while the weave is still loose.
flashcards.answer_line: Shift your hips and pummel the knee between you

plausible: Twist the lower leg out without moving your pelvis
Flatten your back and hold the passer's wrist alone
trap: Extend both knees away from their torso

flashcards.question: Leg Weave defense: why does preserving an upper-body frame matter when your legs are caught?
flashcards.answer: Prevent the passer from flattening your shoulders while controlling the legs.
flashcards.answer_line: It resists the passer flattening your shoulders

plausible: It separates the knees without changing the leg weave
It stops the passer's feet circling without controlling their hips
trap: It substitutes for turning your hips toward the passer

flashcards.question: Leg Weave defense: when can an underhook help you rebuild half guard?
flashcards.answer: An underhook can help you face the passer and rebuild half guard when the shoulder line is not already pinned.
flashcards.answer_line: While your shoulder line still has room to turn

plausible: After both shoulders are pinned with no space to rotate
While both knees stay folded and you face away
trap: Only after you have already cleared all leg contact

flashcards.question: Leg Weave defense: how do you free a knee without wrenching it against the weave?
flashcards.answer: Do not wrench a knee out of a fixed weave; create room with the hips and frames first.
flashcards.answer_line: Create room with frames and move the hip and leg together

plausible: Pull the ankle sideways while the thigh stays pinned
Twist the kneecap outward under the passer's shoulder
trap: Leave your pelvis fixed and kick the foot straight back

flashcards.question: Leg Weave defense: what structure are you trying to preserve between your bodies?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player has a knee shield or comparable leg frame between the bodies.
flashcards.answer_line: A supported knee shield with inside space

plausible: Both knees pressed together beneath the passer's chest
A loose shin with no upper-body frame while the knees fold
trap: Feet pulling the hips close while the knee line stays collapsed

flashcards.question: Leg Weave defense: why does tracking only the passer's weaving arm miss part of the pass?
flashcards.answer: The weaving limb is the passer's arm. The passer still moves the feet and hips to clear the guard, but threading a shin through the legs is not the defining weave in this instruction.
flashcards.answer_line: Their hips and feet still move around your legs

plausible: The arm grip fixes the passer in front of your knees
Keeping the near ankle hooked stops the passer circling either way
trap: Their chest must remain over your hips until the weave opens
